content.comment_body: Hello, is it actually possible that the program I downloaded from [product_name] is not exactly the same as the one that was uploaded? I'm not certain if I used [product_name] [version_no] when uploading, but I definitely used [version_no] when downloading and now for editing the .LSC file. I noticed at least one input behavior changed from 'momentary make' to 'switch', and I'm not sure if there are other changes. The compare tool in [product_name] doesn't show differences like this in the input mode, it only highlights timer differences.
No, the program content remains the same, regardless of whether you use [version_no] for uploading or downloading. What makes you question this?
Because I know that the device wouldn't function correctly if a particular input was set as 'switch'. But the device actually works properly on-site.

I answered too quickly at first. After you updated your initial post, I realized: if you change something like a timer value after uploading and then download the program back to your PC to compare with the original, you will notice differences. However, the setting for whether a digital input acts as a button or a switch is determined by the hardware it's connected to and is not stored in the downloaded program. Selecting 'button' in the properties only affects simulation, so it's only saved in the original program and not transferred to the hardware.
Also, all the names for inputs and outputs disappeared, as well as comments made using the text tool—they're missing from the downloaded program. I assume that's normal?
No, comments and block names are not transferred. Only the actual program code from LSC to [product_name] is sent.

Thanks for confirming, I was on the right track then. I was just a bit unclear in my initial question. I expected that comments and similar data would not be included. Most likely, I made that change to the input myself during testing and just forgot about it.

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion highlights users' confusion about how program transfers work between [product_name] and its associated hardware, particularly regarding version differences, retention of comments, and configuration of input behaviors. Some settings, such as input modes and documentation elements, are not preserved during download, causing misunderstanding. In addition, users note that the comparison tool doesn't always show every configuration difference.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that all settings, including input/output names, remarks, and input configurations, should remain consistent between upload and download processes. They also expect the comparison tool to identify any behavioral or configuration differences between software and hardware versions.
